subjectOf.text: Legal Tech's disruptive innovation combined with the principles of the sharing economy requires lawyers and lawmakers to reevaluate their understanding of many areas of law.
subjectOf.abstract: Legal Tech's disruptive innovation in combination with the principles established by the sharing economy require lawyers and lawmakers to reevaluate their understanding of many areas of the law.

scope_conditions: areas of law touched by sharing and decentralized peer to peer platforms

subjectOf.text: Redesigning legal doctrine around sharing and decentralized peer to peer platforms demands out of the box thinking from a profession whose members were trained, both in law school and across their careers, to think inside the box.
subjectOf.abstract: Such an undertaking requires out-of-the-box thinking for lawyers who were trained during law school and during their entire careers to think inside the box.

subjectOf.text: The sharing economy is defined as the utilization of previously idle services and goods and the partial use of others' property rights in goods, typically coordinated over a platform rather than through centralized employment.
subjectOf.abstract: The sharing economy refers to the utilization of previously idle services and goods and the partial use of others' property rights in goods.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Contemporary Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782198

subjectOf.text: The sharing economy requires a reframing of legacy legal regimes, because the legal frameworks regulating disrupted and adjacent industries are often incompatible with the trends the sharing economy generates.
subjectOf.abstract: The sharing economy necessitates a reframing of legacy legal regimes and frame- works. The legal frameworks that regulate disrupted and associated industries are of- ten incompatible with the emerging trends generated by the sharing economy.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Contemporary Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782198
scope_conditions: applies to regulation of disrupted industries such as transport and lodging

subjectOf.text: The sharing economy outran its legal frameworks: the legal regimes governing the disrupted industries were often incompatible with the trends the sharing economy generated, forcing cities and municipalities into a proactive regulatory stance.
subjectOf.abstract: The legal frameworks that regulate disrupted and associated industries were often incompatible with the emerging trends generated by the sharing economy.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859
scope_conditions: applies to ridesharing and homesharing regulation at city and state level
